terms.meaning: A reference record that names a source, its link, and when it was accessed.
A short code calculated from a longer text, used as a quick identifier.
A pointer to the exact place in a source, such as a page or section.

sections.name: UpdateInput
sections.title: Shape of an update input
sections.what: Describes the fields an update may contain, with most of them optional.
sections.why: Lets the mapper accept updates from different places that fill fields differently.
sections.watch_out: Several date fields exist, but the citation only uses the basic date, so other dates are ignored.

sections.name: Citation
sections.title: Shape of a citation
sections.what: Describes the fields a citation holds, such as id, title, link, publisher, and excerpt.
sections.why: Gives all citations one consistent shape.

sections.name: stableId
sections.title: Stable identifier from date and headline
sections.what: Builds a short, repeatable id from the date and headline so the same update always gets the same id.
sections.why: A repeatable id lets the app recognize the same citation again.
sections.watch_out: Identical date and headline pairs share an id.

sections.name: updateToCitation
sections.title: Converting an update into a citation
sections.what: Turns one update into a citation, using a default title when the headline is empty and an empty link when none exists.
sections.why: Lets updates appear next to other sources in the same format.
sections.watch_out: The source is used as both the source name and the publisher, so they always match.

summary: Turns a project update into a citation, the kind of reference card used to show where a fact came from.
purpose: Lets update entries appear in the same citation format as other sources.
why: Reason not stated in the code. It gives every update a stable identifier and a fallback title.
how: Builds a short id from the date and headline using a simple hash, then copies the headline, link, source, date, excerpt, and locator into the citation shape. Missing values get safe defaults.
inputs: An update with date, headline, source, optional link, excerpt, and locator.
outputs: A citation with an id, title, link, publisher, access date, excerpt, and locator.
risks: Two updates with the same date and headline get the same id. The hash can collide in rare cases.
debug: If two citations clash, compare their dates and headlines. If a citation has no link, check the update's url field.
